=== PMID: 27510704 ===

Title: Atrial natriuretic peptide induces peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ during cardiac ischemia-reperfusion in swine heart.

Journal/Date: General thoracic and cardiovascular surgery (2017)

MeSH Keywords: Animals, Atrial Natriuretic Factor, Disease Models, Animal, Hemodynamics, Myocardial Reperfusion Injury, Myocardium, PPAR gamma, Swine


--- ABSTRACT ---
[OBJECTIVES]: Atrial natriuretic peptide is a cardiac atrium-derived hormone and its cardioprotective effects have recently been confirmed, but the actual mechanism underlying these effects has not been well elucidated. In this study, we proposed that atrial natriuretic peptide achieves its effects in part via peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ, a nuclear receptor.
[METHODS]: Hemodynamic data in swine heart ischemia-reperfusion model were measured under the conditions of no medication for control (Group N, n = 8) or that of carperitide (synthetic human atrial natriuretic peptide) systemic administration (Group A, n = 8). After 30 min of left anterior descending artery total occlusion and 4 h of reperfusion, peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ mRNA and protein expressions in cardiac muscle were examined. The mRNA expression of Liver X receptor α, the downstream agent of peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ, was also evaluated. Creatine kinase-myocardial band and Troponin T elevations after reperfusion were evaluated as markers of cardiac damage.
[RESULTS]: The dP/dT decrease during reperfusion was ameliorated in Group A. Peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ mRNA expression in Group A was significantly higher in ischemic area than that in Group N, although the difference was not significant in the marginal and non-ischemic areas. The peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ protein expression in ischemic area was also significantly dominant in Group A.
[CONCLUSIONS]: Atrial natriuretic peptide may achieve its cardioprotective effects in part via the activation of the peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ pathway, particularly in central areas of ischemic lesions.

key_findings.finding: The directly relevant primary study is PMID 27510704 (2017), using a swine cardiac ischemia–reperfusion model: pigs received no medication (n=8) or systemic carperitide, synthetic human ANP (n=8), followed by 30-minute total LAD occlusion and 4-hour reperfusion. PPARγ mRNA and protein were measured in cardiac muscle. In the ischemic area, PPARγ mRNA was significantly higher with carperitide than control, and PPARγ protein expression was also significantly greater; differences in marginal and non-ischemic areas were not significant.

source_tools.relevance: Identifies the primary study and reports model, intervention, timing, tissue, outcomes, and regional results.

key_findings.finding: Because the study compared experimentally administered carperitide with untreated controls, it supports ANP-treatment-associated induction of PPARγ in ischemic myocardium rather than a purely observational association. However, the abstract supports an increase in expression, not proof that PPARγ mediates ANP cardioprotection or that ANP directly activates PPARγ; the authors state this pathway may contribute.

source_tools.relevance: Abstract reports intervention-control comparison and authors' qualified conclusion on pathway mediation.
